messages:
Marcus: Oxbow Health returned their netops checklist. POC will call hosted API but compliance requires private connectivity. They asked whether PrivateLink or peering is better, need firewall entries, and want static IPs only.
Zoe: Short: PrivateLink can work for IP-only if we provision the interface endpoint and share the endpoint ENI public IPs. Note: AWS may reassign underlying EIPs during maintenance. For immutable IPs suggest peering or Dedicated.
Dina: Also call out: PrivateLink does NOT preserve original client source IP for traffic once it reaches our backend. If they need src-IP preservation for downstream ACLs, peering or deploying Redwood in their account is required.
Marcus: They explicitly said no DNS/SNI allowlist, only IPs. Timeline: POC starts next Tuesday. Can infra stand up a sandbox quickly?
Leila: ops-bot will kick this off once we confirm. Minimal firewall snippet for their change ticket: 
```
{"rule_name":"oxbow->redwood-privatelink","direction":"egress","proto":"tcp","port":"443","dest":"<REPLACE_WITH_PROVIDED_EIP>","purpose":"POC to Redwood Inference"}
```
Zoe: Also include optional rules for PMTU and NTP: Allow ICMP type 3 (PMTU) and UDP/123 to NTP if they don't manage time internally.
Dina: Security answers to questionnaire: TLS 1.2/1.3 in transit; mTLS only for Dedicated/private deployments; request-level logging and audit trails available in Console. I'll draft the network section.
ops-bot: Created ticket NET-33120 to provision sandbox PrivateLink in us-east-1 for Oxbow POC. ETA: 48 hours.
Marcus: Great. Action items: (1) I'll tell Oxbow we'll provide EIPs after provisioning and ask for change window approval, (2) Dina will paste security bullets into the questionnaire, (3) Leila confirm infra ticket owner and ETA.
Leila: Confirmed owner is infra-oncall. Will update ticket with EIP list once ready. If Oxbow pushes for src-IP preservation escalate to me (we may propose peering or short Dedicated eval).
